# Google Ads for Dentists: The Complete 2026 Guide

You can't reach everyone who needs dental services by relying on referrals. Google Ads lets you intercept patients when they're actively searching for a dentist. This guide covers campaign setup, keyword research, ad copy, and tracking, based on experience managing dental campaigns since 2007.

## Why Google Ads Works for Dental Practices

Google Ads allows you to reach a highly targeted audience. With advanced targeting options, you can show your ads to people actively searching for dental services in your area. Your ads are seen by the right people at the right time, increasing the likelihood of a booking.

Unlike radio, TV, or word-of-mouth, you can track performance in real time. You'll see how many clicks your ads receive, how many conversions they generate, and how much you spend per click. You'll identify your most profitable patients and focus on the keywords driving them to book.

For one of our cosmetic dentistry clients, we were able to start reliably generating **35-40 high-quality leads every single day**. That's what a properly structured dental campaign can achieve.

## Which Campaign Types Work for Dentists?

**Search campaigns** are the starting point. They reach people while they're actively searching for a dentist. You identify the right keywords and create ads explaining why they should choose your practice.

![Example Google Ads search result for a dental practice showing headline structure and ad extensions](/images/dental/google-ads-for-dentists-example.jpg)

**Display campaigns** work for remarketing, showing ads to people who visited your website but didn't book. These are lower cost and effective at bringing back undecided patients.

We typically recommend starting with Search, then layering in remarketing once you have enough traffic data.

## Keyword Research for Dental Campaigns

Start with broad keywords describing your services: "dentist," "dental clinic," "teeth whitening." Then narrow them down through research to find the keywords you _should_ target: "cosmetic dentist for veneers," "dental implant specialist," "emergency dentist \[city\]."

![Google Ads example showing a well-structured dental practice ad with specific treatment keywords](/images/dental/great-google-ad-for-dentists-example.jpg)

Generic "dentist near me" searches are expensive and attract low-intent browsers. Terms like "cost of veneers in \[city\]," "how long does Invisalign take," and "is dental implant surgery painful" reveal high intent and strong motivation. Focus your budget there.

Use tools like Google Keyword Planner, SpyFu, or Semrush. Don't just target what seems obvious. Check what your competitors are bidding on, and look for gaps they're missing.

## Campaign Structure That Works

Separate ad groups (and sometimes separate campaigns) for each service line:

*   **Dental implants**: highest value, highest CPC, needs dedicated budget
*   **Cosmetic dentistry**: veneers, whitening, Invisalign
*   **General dentistry**: check-ups, cleanings, fillings
*   **Emergency dentistry**: urgent care, same-day appointments

Each patient type sees an ad that speaks to their specific need instead of a generic list of treatments. This improves Quality Score, reduces CPC, and increases conversion rates.

## Tracking What Matters

![Google Ads conversion tracking dashboard showing dental practice lead metrics](/images/dental/google-ads-for-dentists-example-02.jpg)

"Getting leads" means nothing if patients don't sit in your chair. We track:

*   **Phone calls**: attributed to specific keywords and ads
*   **Form submissions**: booked consultations
*   **CRM integration**: which leads become confirmed treatments

When Google Ads knows which keywords generate actual patients (not just form fills), it optimises towards those keywords. Most dental practices miss this step.

## Landing Pages That Convert

Your landing page should be crafted specifically for each service. The message that brought them in must be front and centre, creating a straight line towards the booking. Key elements:

*   Headline matching the ad they clicked
*   Trust signals: years of experience, patient reviews, before/after photos
*   A clear, prominent booking form or phone number
*   Specific information about the treatment they searched for

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How much do Google Ads cost for dentists?

Cost per click for dental keywords typically ranges from $3 to $20, depending on procedure and location. Dental implant keywords are the most expensive. As of 2026, most dental practices we work with generate leads at $15-$60 each, depending on the treatment type.

### Should I advertise all my services at once?

Start with your highest-value services. If dental implants generate the most revenue per patient, start there. Get that campaign profitable, then expand into cosmetic, general, and emergency.

### How quickly will I see results?

Most dental campaigns start generating enquiries within 2-3 weeks. The first 60-90 days are an optimisation period. One of our clients went from zero to 35-40 leads per day once the campaign was fully optimised.

A dental clinic can leverage [the latest technological advances](https://www.getweave.com/industry/dentistry/) to manage its operations, but a small business can suffer from a lack of clients and cash flow. The problem can lie in essential factors such as weak customer service, long average waiting time, bad appointment planning, or a lack of effective teeth-whitening advertising.

While every issue can be fixed or corrected promptly, the last factor is the hardest of all to improve and of utmost importance. Imagine your future long-term prospective patient looking for a dentist at this very moment on the internet, but your dental office website can be buried somewhere on the second or third page of a search engine. If you need better teeth whitening promotion ideas to reach new patients, it is time to upgrade your strategy.

Although developing your online presence is a lengthy process, it is worth it. Before exploring how to get started with successful teeth whitening ads, remember to set clear, realistic goals and expectations.

## 1\. Social Media Marketing

While having a website is a necessity, running a social media account for your dental office is a must. It is an indispensable tool that will drive sales and bring new patients to your dental clinic. Besides, you will be able to get in touch with your patients, read their concerns and react accordingly, answer their questions, and run various dental ads.

Most and foremost, to effectively strategize dental marketing, you should analyze and determine your target audience for teeth whitening. It cannot be everyone who wants to receive dental care, but a group of people of a certain age, gender, and residence, among other characteristics.

Your social media can assist you in broadcasting limited promotions, informing patients about a new dental service, and promoting social media posts with engaging and useful information about dental care in your clinic.

Social media platforms like Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok are used by millions of people. And this is your opportunity to grab their attention and elevate your presence. You should use Facebook to keep the latest information about your business: location, contact details, working hours, and latest promotions.

Instagram is famous for sharing photos and videos, and you could upload before-and-after results of teeth whitening treatment or dental hygiene, add high-quality products that you use to perform procedures, and share behind-the-scenes secrets to intrigue your viewers. Similar to Instagram, TikTok is a platform for short clips, and there, your skilled dentists could share little-known tips about toothaches and tips on how to care for teeth. Whichever platform you plan to use for a successful dental marketing campaign, make sure to adjust your content.

## 2\. Reviews

Writing a blog post as a part of your dental marketing can be very educational for your existing clients, but it might not convert potential patients into long-term clients. Therefore, the best way to prove your dental clinic is a go-to place for any kind of dental procedure [is to get reviews from real people](https://www.getweave.com/weave-marketing/). It will earn you credibility and trustworthiness online.

According to NRC Health, 83.3% of patients value online reviews more than personal recommendations when deciding on using the services of certain healthcare providers.¹

![According to NRC Health, 83.3% of patients value online reviews more than personal recommendations](https://live-getweave.pantheonsite.io/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/According-to-NRC-Health-83.3-of-patients-value-online-reviews-more-than-personal-recommendations-300x171.png)

Importance of online reviews for dental practice (Source: NRC Health)

Another set of statistics, yet again, proves that reviews on Facebook, Yelp, and Google do play a big role in a buying decision. The pivotal factors that influence potential customers to use your services are the positive reviews, star ratings, and your company’s engagement with commenters. Moreover, recency matters a lot, so if you haven’t had any feedback in the past month, it can divert customers away from your clinic.

Want teeth whitening marketing ideas? Ask about Weave Reviews

#### 9 out of 10 people check online reviews before choosing a business

  

Weave helps you easily collect and monitor reviews on Google and Facebook. These reviews can be some of the best marketing for your business.

Sometimes excellent customer care is much appreciated but not enough – this is when you equip your office staff with coupons and bonuses. Give your clients a small discount or a free procedure as a “thank you” for leaving a comment, as much-needed encouragement. Consequently, dental marketing can be performed both online and on-site.

More often than not, people check information about certain places on Google, or better said, they Google it. Therefore, having up-to-date information about your cosmetic dentistry will help customers find you or read more about your offers.
